extracted.intended_audience: Navy Contracting Officers and DoD procurement professionals implementing OMB Circular A-76 / CITA contracting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for Contracting Officers implementing OMB Circular A-76 in Commercial or Industrial Type Activity (CITA) support service procurements, covering the cost-comparison process, Phase I/II/III framework, solicitation/evaluation/award issues, and related administrative matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison process (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost comparison process is the cornerstone of CITA support service contracting and distinguishes it from other service contracting efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process commences with establishment of a Task Group to prepare an overall plan, SOW, and acquisition schedule; solicit bids/proposals; prepare and audit an in-house Government cost estimate (sealed and submitted); determine low contract price; adjust contract price to reflect true Government cost; conduct cost comparison; certify and audit the comparison; possibly conduct pre-award survey; prepare recommendations to the Approving Authority; announce results and allow public review; then award contract or cancel solicitation. (Exhibit I outlines responsibilities and sequence: TG, CO, IA, AA, PC.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Group establishment and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a Task Group (TG) to prepare an overall plan to obtain the desired service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TG initial responsibilities include establishment of an acquisition schedule and development of a detailed statement of work (SOW); preparing the in-house Government cost estimate; submitting the sealed in-house estimate; conducting the cost comparison; completing and certifying the cost comparison; preparing decision summary recommendations for the Approving Authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer responsibilities in the cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer (CO) issues solicitations, determines low contract price, conducts pre-award surveys, announces results and manages public review, and carries out contract award or cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CO must issue solicitations to prospective contractors, determine the low 'contract price', adjust contract price (see separate metric), conduct pre-award survey if industry cost appears lower, announce results of cost study to the public and allow time for review, and after review award contract or cancel the solicitation. CO is responsible for maintaining the integrity of the overall process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government in‑house cost estimate: audit, seal, submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare an in-house Government cost estimate to perform the same service as solicited contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Government cost estimate is audited for accuracy and conformance to prescribed guidelines, sealed, and submitted to the Contracting Officer. The timing of submission and potential late submission should be managed (see Award-cycle guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust contract price to reflect true cost to the Government
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining the comparative cost of private-sector performance, adjust the contractor's 'contract price' to reflect the true cost to the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of the cost comparison it is necessary to adjust the 'contract price' to reflect the true cost to the Government for private sector performance; the total adjusted private-sector cost is then compared with the in-house Government cost estimate to determine an apparent winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit/certification of cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The Task Group must complete and certify the cost comparison and it must be subjected to an independent audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After completion of the cost comparison the TG completes and certifies it; the comparison is again subjected to an audit. Discrepancies resulting from verification and audit may present potential problems and must be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award survey criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a pre-award survey when the total private industry cost appears lower than the Government in-house cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If private industry cost appears lower, the Contracting Officer may conduct a pre-award survey on the lower offeror to verify capability prior to award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice requirement (CBD notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before retaining a function in-house based on nonavailability of commercial sources, agencies must make the requirement known broadly via Commerce Business Daily (CBD) notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a minimum, place at least three notices of the requirements in the Commerce Business Daily over a 90-day period; for urgent requirements publication can be reduced to two notices over a 30-day period. Notices need not state they are being issued pursuant to the Circular. CBD responses only indicate 'availability' and do not require contractors to demonstrate capability, creating evidentiary limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informational solicitations and market surveys: limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Informational solicitations and market surveys can help determine interest but have distinct disadvantages and are insufficient alone to establish nonavailability of commercial sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors may not invest time or expense to respond to information-only notices, and responses may be poorly prepared; informational solicitations do not guarantee all potential sources are aware of the requirement. Market surveys (e.g., via SBA, GSA) should be used in addition. Priced informational solicitations are unacceptable as the basis for using the 'lower in-house cost' exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for sufficiency of CBD responses (availability determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular is ambiguous as to how many responses constitute sufficient interest to establish commercial availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literal interpretation suggests availability of even one source would preclude use of the 'nonavailability' exception, but existing directives are silent on numeric thresholds; extensive documentation is required to justify in‑house performance based on nonavailability (e.g., capacity or technical competence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for determining commercial nonavailability
rubrics_metrics.description: Who initially determines that no commercial source is available—CO or functional activity—is unclear, but practical and theoretical considerations favor the Contracting Officer making the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Development of sources of supply is generally CO's realm; therefore the decision should typically rest with the Contracting Officer, though practice varies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: preparation of the C/I inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an inventory of Commercial or Industrial Type (C/I) activities as part of Phase I assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory preparation supports identification of functions for possible review and conversion and is a foundational Phase I activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: establishment of review schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish schedules for review of functions to determine potential conversion to contract performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review schedules govern which functions are reviewed in a given fiscal year and affect opportunities for consolidation across activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: justification for in‑house performance based on National Defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Document and justify retention of in-house performance when national defense considerations require it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Defense justification is an acceptable basis for in‑house retention and must be clearly documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: justification for in‑house performance based on nonavailability of commercial sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare justification for retaining functions in-house due to lack of suitable commercial sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires detailed documentation that private firms lack sufficient capacity or technical competence; CBD notices and other outreach must be shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: preparation and submission of fact sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare and submit fact sheets summarizing the function and rationale for review or retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact sheets support internal decision-making and external communications (e.g., reporting to oversight bodies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: grouping of similar functions for larger solicitation packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Group similar functions to create larger, more attractive solicitation packages for contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouping can enhance contractor interest and permit cost savings; the CO can advise functional activities on grouping strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: consideration of multifunctional (umbrella) solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider umbrella or multifunctional solicitations (e.g., Base Operation Support Service/BOSS contracts) to cover multiple base support functions under a single contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: potential lower total price, reduced solicitation/administration costs, centralized management. Disadvantages: turbulent phase-in/turnover, start-up coordination problems, greater complexity in conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: determination of core capability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify core capability requirements that must be retained in-house or are essential to mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of core capabilities informs what can be contracted out and what must remain Government-operated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: preparation of local implementing directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare local directives to implement agency and DoD/A-76 policy in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local implementing directives translate higher-level policy into actionable procedures for contracting offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: explore utilization of excess capacity at other Government agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether excess capacity at other Government agencies can satisfy requirements instead of contracting out or retaining in-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter-agency utilization may be an alternative to private-sector contracting and should be evaluated during Phase I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: communications with interested parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and manage communications with interested parties throughout Phase I and the entire process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication procedures must account for the sensitive nature of CITA reviews and restrictions on supplying information to interested persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II planning considerations (organizational)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address internal organizational considerations in Phase II planning, including workload impacts, staffing, training, Procurement Administrative Lead Time (PALT), and contracting authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These managerial issues affect readiness to implement policy and require assessment before solicitation reaches the contracting office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition (Phase II) contracting considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: During contracting sub-phase, attention to solicitation methods, sources of supply (including small and disadvantaged businesses), DAR coverage and clause selection, contract type determination, and use of options is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COs should review pre-solicitation issues closely and ensure selection of appropriate contract type, clauses, and consideration of socio-economic sourcing objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation and evaluation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-examine use of pre-bid and pre-proposal conferences, negotiation methods (especially when the Government is an offeror), philosophies of competition, and revised methodologies to evaluate contractor proposals including incentive arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Government may be a competitor, negotiation techniques and evaluation criteria may need adjustment; incentive arrangements and evaluation methodologies must fairly compare in-house and private offers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award-cycle issues and public review
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between solicitation evaluation factors and contract award factors; manage timing and disclosure of the in-house cost estimate; conduct preliminary and final announcements and allow required public review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address possible late submission of the in-house estimate, determine correct time to reveal the estimate to the public, ensure compliance with public review requirements, and understand appeals versus the protest process. Verification and audit discrepancies must be managed before final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-type contract special requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Service contracts pose unique challenges: ensure services are nonpersonal, include Service Contract Act wage/fringe provisions, consider use of options, prepare longer/more complex SOWs, and provide for performance measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COs must structure contracts to avoid creating employer-employee relationships, include mandated clauses on wages/fringes, plan for options to extend performance, develop provisions to measure contractor progress and performance (since no end item may exist), and consider site visits if work is on Government facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract administration phase considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract Administration (Phase III) commences with award and continues for the contract duration; plan for surveillance, performance standards, delegation, and phase-in issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish surveillance plans and performance standards tied to the SOW, determine delegation of contract administration responsibilities (e.g., DCASOs), and account for phase-in/turnover issues in milestone planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advantages and disadvantages of multifunctional/umbrella contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate tradeoffs for umbrella contracts: potential cost and administrative savings vs greater risk during conversion and phase-in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature and examples (e.g., BSSC at Bangor) indicate potential for lower total price, reduced solicitation/administration cost, centralized management, and communication benefits; main disadvantage is turbulent phase-in/turnover with coordination and start-up difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of identical functions across activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize and centralize review schedules and consolidate same-type functions across activities to enable single large solicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation permits coordinated development of work statements/specifications and can improve contractor interest and performance (example: consolidated janitorial contracts in San Diego). Centralization decisions may be constrained by higher-level scheduling (e.g., CNO determinations) and congressional notice requirements.
